newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CANOEING-CHEESEMAN THROWS DOWN BERG GAUNTLET.
newsitem.headline: CANOEING-CHEESEMAN THROWS DOWN BERG GAUNTLET.

text.p: Gauteng doctor Michael Cheeseman stamped his authority on the Berg River canoe marathon with victory over the 59.1 km first stage from Paarl to Zonqasdrift on Wednesday.
The 29-year-old, who was runner-up in 1996, finished more than three minutes ahead of his nearest challenger on the opening morning of the four-day race.
Cheeseman took advantage of tree blocks to surge clear of South African canoe marathon champion and co-favourite Graham Bird, who eventually finished 13 minutes behind the winner in ninth place.

He also dropped Paul Marais and Murray Wilson who paddled in together in second and third places to open up a healthy lead in the race to succeed six time winner Robbie Herreveld, who has opted not to paddle this year.

In the women's race Jean Wilson, who won the fourth of her titles under her maiden name of Yates in 1996, took a two minute lead over capsize victim Antje Malherbe -- who won the title in 1995 as Antje Manfroni, a year Wilson was absent.
1. Michael Cheesman four hours 16 minutes 59 seconds
